source.title: Fermanagh Herald, 10 June 1967, p. 7 ("Fermanagh's new County Council is elected"); Irish News, 2 June 1967, p. 8 ("Poll in Enniskillen")
source.publisher: Fermanagh Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Votes as printed; 75 per cent poll.

note: First election of the new amalgamated Fermanagh County Council (county council, Enniskillen Borough Council and the Enniskillen, Irvinestown and Lisnaskea Rural Councils), polled Thursday 1 June 1967 (Fermanagh Herald, 3 June 1967, polling-day advertisement: 'POLLING DAY - THURSDAY, 1st JUNE, 1967'). Five divisions were nominated as contests (Crom, Doon, Irvinestown, Roslea and Enniskillen North) for twelve of the fifty seats; the other seventeen divisions were uncontested and the Herald of 20 May 1967 prints the full nomination list, so their members are recorded here. Crom did not go to a poll: the result report counts only four contests (Fermanagh Herald, 10 June 1967, p. 7: 'In only one case, of the four contests') and the first meeting names both Eamon O'Reilly and Hugh Reilly as members (Fermanagh Herald, 24 June 1967, p. 7), so the two Reillys were returned and James Watterson, the third nominee, did not take a seat. Structure and division names for the 1966-67 amalgamation are in notes/fermanagh-fcra-1969.md, from Fermanagh CRA, 'Fermanagh Facts' (1969). That is an advocacy pamphlet: use it for names only, not figures. Its register figures are disputed by Kingsley (2021) on the Omagh Rural District scheme. Read the page image before recording any number from it.
